prompt: Help me learn area and perimeter. Compare two rectangles: A is 6 metres wide and 4 metres high; B is 8 metres wide and 2 metres high. They should start with the same perimeter. Put them side by side, give each its own width and height controls, and show area and perimeter for each.

request.prompt: Help me learn area and perimeter. Compare two rectangles: A is 6 metres wide and 4 metres high; B is 8 metres wide and 2 metres high. They should start with the same perimeter. Put them side by side, give each its own width and height controls, and show area and perimeter for each.

recipe.title: Area & perimeter
recipe.description: Change the side lengths. Watch area and perimeter respond.

lesson.title: Area & perimeter
lesson.instruction: Change the side lengths. Watch area and perimeter respond.
lesson.explanation:
Side lengths describe a rectangle in metres and range from 0.1 to 100. Area is width times height in square metres; perimeter is twice their sum in metres. The drawing preserves the side-length proportion while adapting its scale to fit.
Area of rectangle A is 6m * 4m = 24m². Area of rectangle B is 8m * 2m = 16m². Both rectangles start with the same perimeter, which is 2*(6m + 4m) = 20m. Changing dimensions affects area and perimeter proportionally.
